justifications.decision: The compound is masculine nominative singular and suits the first-person subject of pṛcchāmi/aham, not an independent subject ‘nature’. The internal relation is instrumental/causal: the svabhāva is upahata by the kārpaṇya-doṣa. MW supports svabhāva as ‘nature, innate disposition’ and upa-√han as ‘hurt, damage, afflict, impede, spoil’.
options_considered: bahuvrīhi qualifying the speaker: ‘whose nature is impaired by the fault of weakness’
tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya taken as an independent nominative: ‘the nature impaired by the fault of weakness’
justifications.chosen: kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ is a bahuvrīhi: ‘one whose own disposition has been impaired by the fault of kārpaṇya’.

justifications.decision: The compound is masculine nominative singular and qualifies the speaker. The natural vigraha is dharme saṃmūḍhaṃ ceto yasya: cetas is the inner head, saṃmūḍha describes the mind’s bewilderment, and dharma marks the matter about which the mind is confused. MW supports dharma as duty/right/prescribed conduct and sam-√muh as being stupefied or bewildered.
options_considered: ‘a mind bewildered by dharma as agent’
justifications.chosen: dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetāḥ is a bahuvrīhi: ‘one whose mind is bewildered concerning dharma’.

justifications.decision: yat is nominative neuter singular in the relative clause with syāt, śreyaḥ is the neuter predicate/substantive ‘the better thing, higher good’, and tat is the neuter accusative object of brūhi. me is the dative recipient, ‘to me’.
options_considered: relative-correlative construction: yat … tat, with tat as object of brūhi
taking yat itself as the direct object of brūhi across the clause
taking me as genitive ‘of me’ rather than dative ‘to me’
justifications.chosen: yac chreyaḥ syāt … tan me brūhi is relative-correlative: ‘what would be the higher good, tell that to me’.

justifications.decision: Although niścitam could formally be read as a neuter accusative adjective, MW explicitly gives niścitam as an indeclinable meaning ‘decidedly, positively’. Its placement before brūhi naturally gives the force ‘tell for certain’.
options_considered: accusative adjective modifying tat: ‘tell that certain thing’
justifications.chosen: niścitam is adverbial with brūhi: ‘tell decisively/for certain’.

justifications.decision: te is genitive singular with śiṣyaḥ. prapannam is masculine accusative singular agreeing with mām, while tvām is the object governed by pra-√pad, ‘resort to, take refuge with’ (MW s.v. pra-√pad). śādhi, from √śās, is therefore best translated ‘instruct’ here rather than merely ‘rule’.
options_considered: ‘I am your disciple; instruct me, who have taken refuge in you’
‘I am to be taught by you’ with śiṣya primarily adjectival
taking prapannam with tvām: ‘you, who are surrendered’
justifications.chosen: śiṣyas te ’ham means ‘I am your disciple/pupil’, and śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam means ‘instruct me, who have taken refuge in you’.

translation:
With my own disposition stricken by the fault of weakness (kārpaṇya),
with my mind bewildered about duty (dharma), I ask you:
what would be the higher good (śreyas)—tell that to me decisively.
I am your disciple; instruct me, who have taken refuge in you.
one_shot_delta: Since no commentary text is supplied for this unit, the main risks are grammatical and lexical rather than commentarial.
A quick translation might render kārpaṇya literally as ‘poverty’ or ‘miserliness’; here the context favors ‘weakness/poor-spiritedness’.
It might miss the bahuvrīhi force of kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ and dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetāḥ, both qualifying Arjuna/the speaker.
It might take niścitam as ‘the certain good’ rather than the adverbial ‘tell me decisively/for certain’.
It might attach prapannam to tvām, but grammatically it agrees with mām: ‘me, having taken refuge in you’.
analyzer_disagreements: The tagger marked me as genitive singular (mad_SG); here it is taken as dative singular because it is the recipient with brūhi, ‘tell to me’.
The tagger left niścitam without a full inflectional analysis; it is taken as an indeclinable adverb, following MW s.v. niścitam: ‘decidedly, positively’.
The tagger reports prapannam under the verbal root prapad as a past participial form; per the requested schema it is represented as a subanta from the participial stem prapanna, Pum Dvitiya Eka.

The tagger’s first- and second-person pronoun analyses do not mark linga; masculine is supplied contextually for Arjuna/the speaker and Kṛṣṇa/the addressee, while keeping their case and number stable.
